items.title: Former Dragon Age boss questions whether BioWare should have become 'a one project studio' dropping either Mass Effect or Dragon Age to survive EA
items.summary:
Many are asking themselves how a legendary studio like BioWare, which is responsible for staples of the PC gaming genre like Neverwinter Nights , Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic , and the OG Baldur's Gate , alongside Mass Effect and Dragon Age , can be shuttered. 

Former Dragon Age executive producer Mark Darrah has already explained how the studio was backed into a corner by EA. Escalating financial pressure led to the poor decisions and subpar games we saw ahead of BioWare's closure. But what if it had all gone differently? Despite everything, Darrah does question whether there was a way for BioWare to survive under EA.

(Image credit: EA) "BioWare's entire existence under EA—it was essentially zero sum, if somebody was getting resources it was coming at the expense of somebody else," Darrah explains. "It's almost like BioWare has run exactly the same way for its entire existence. But the external constraints were different. So in the early days when BioWare needed more people it hired more people. That's like Baldur's Gate 1, Neverwinter Nights, in the early days when we have all these different threads and branches. 

"And then in 2007/2008, when the EA constraints come in, the same desires are there, we need more people to ship our games so the way we fix that in that time period is by cutting off all those other branches. So [Jade Empire sequel] Revolver goes away and the Handheld [Development] Group goes away … and so Dragon Age and Mass Effect eats everything." 

The alternative? Scaling things down to meet EA's needs. "Budgets keep going up, but we're…
items.t: Former Dragon Age boss questions whether BioWare should have become 'a one project studio' dropping either Mass Effect or Dragon Age to survive EA

Cyberleek released a near-complete build of GTA 6 late last week, holding back only the main exe—the part that makes everything else run, basically—until either their crypto coin achieved a $15 million market cap, or November 23, whichever came first. The crypto missed badly, but time marches on, and so here we are.

(Image credit: Cyberleek) The release of the exe, naturally, includes a call for more "donations" in its readme file (via Reddit ) which Cyberleek said will go toward a secretive project "for the gamers." They also taunted Take-Two Interactive's efforts to track them down : "Months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving. No budget makes a lock unbreakable, and no court order deletes what the internet already has."

Leaks in the game industry aren't anything new, but this case is unique: GTA 6, effectively the biggest videogame of all time, still hasn't been announced for PC, as is Take-Two's way . But the advent of AI means the game could be emulated on our platform far more quickly than was possible in the past—some modders estimated it could happen within a week.

The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak in September 2022 has been released on license with a strong warning from the judge. Having already served the majority of his seven year sentence, Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford in the United Kingdom, was allowed to go free, conditionally. 

According to the BBC , the judge warned Kurtaj: "Don't let this happen again."

Kurtaj attempted to extort GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games in 2022. After socially engineering his way into the company Slack, the now 21-year-old threatened to release clips of the unfinished game unless Rockstar paid a ransom. He pleaded guilty to the hacking offenses , which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, earlier this week.

The next 50% require, well, a lot of nook-scouring and cranny-uncovering—many more hours of gameplay which I am preserving for myself as a Christmas holiday treat.

And when I do, I suspect I might make a little (just a little) use of this rad Queen's Domain map by a creator called Leny15 . Barely a week ago I wrote that "I suspect a cross-section of [Queen's Domain's] goliath, entwined map would make for a killer bit of wall art". Well, I was right. Here it is and it looks rad as hell.

No, really. Even if you're not a Queen's Domain player—or maybe especially if you're not—take a look at this thing. items.title: 60 hours in GTA 6 has me yearning for an online Leonida
items.summary:
I honestly can't recall the last time I took such delight in existing within a virtual world as the way I have with Grand Theft Auto 6 's Leonida. Rockstar has delivered on its promise of both breadth and depth—the map is huge, but utterly stuffed with detail. Large, open highways shrink into single lanes surrounded by construction that force me to slam the brakes. Sidewalks sparse with pedestrians eventually lead to densely packed retail areas, restaurants, and clubs. 

Pockets of culture erupt all over: the sheer redneckery of Port Gellhorn, the Latin culture that permeates Little Cuba, and the affluent snootiness of Capri that has cops flinging microaggressions in every direction. You don't need to undertake any missions in these areas to understand the people that live here—Rockstar has nailed so much of the environmental storytelling and the conversations between NPCs you'll stumble on as you roam.

(Image credit: Rockstar Games) It's a world that, when I first ventured into it, I had no interest in exploring in a multiplayer setting. I spent an ungodly amount of time in GTA 5's Online mode when it first released. I was there on the ground for its incredibly shaky launch (I made a character and then got stuck in that birdseye view loading screen for hours, incredible stuff) and continued to sink time into it over the years, particularly during Covid.

And I like it well enough, but its novelty has waned over the last decade. Its core experience is inherently different from what singleplayer brings, and I had yearned to return to a world less about blowing other…

items.title: Do You Need the Key Cloner to Steal All of GTA 6's Cars?
items.summary:
Throughout your early hours in GTA 6, you may have been faced with many vehicles that you simply aren’t equipped to steal. It can be frustrating to walk up to a nice-looking car and be faced with the prospect of not being able to drive away in it because a “key cloner” is needed. Even if some oblivious rich person happens to leave their driver’s seat door open for you to slip into, you’ll still need the required tech to start the engine. Instead, you’ll have to wait until you can start cloning keys until you can experience the full range of Vice City vehicles available to you. Here’s when you’ll get it, and how it works.

GTA 6 smartly staggers what class of car is available to you over the course of its story, minimising the risk that comes with jacking them as Jason and Lucia become smarter criminals. At first, you’ll be limited to rusty work vehicles and family sedans, but even these come with a risk. You’ll either have to steal them from somebody already driving, thus risking them alerting the cops to your crimes, or smash through a window to gain access, which is likely to raise an alarm.

Your handy “Waink” scanner app on your phone can help you work out which vehicles you should be targeting. Those with the “key cloner” symbol attached to them are pointless to go after until partway through chapter three, which we’ll get onto soon. It’s not even until chapter two, and you meet Moses, that you’ll even be able to get into low-level cars easily. items.title: Daredevil Star Charlie Cox Asked for a James Bond Audition but Was Told He Was 'Too Old'
items.summary:
Daredevil star Charlie Cox says he was denied a James Bond audition after being told he was already "too old" to play 007, prior to the casting of Twilight and Batman star Robert Pattinson .

Despite spending the past decade throwing himself into brutal hallway brawls, Cox said he couldn't even audition to be the new James Bond because of his age. Speaking today on Virgin Radio , the 43-year-old Marvel star said he'd asked his agent about becoming the new 00 agent, only to be quickly shut down.

"I asked to audition for that, do you know what they told me? Too old," Cox laughed, admitting that he didn't even make it into an audition room. "Rob's the same age as me!" he continued, before being told that, actually, the Batman actor is three years younger.

"What an amazing career that guy's carved out," Cox said, praising Pattinson for getting the part. "Some of the stuff he's done, the directors he's worked with... just amazing."

While Cox wouldn't have been the oldest actor cast as James Bond, he would have certainly been on the older end. Sean Connery was 32 years old when he gained 007 status, George Lazenby was 30 years old, Roger Moore was 45 years old, Timothy Dalton was 41 years old, Pierce Brosnan was 42 years old, and Daniel Craig was 38 years old. 

Still, for fans who have watched Cox effortlessly pull off both sharp-suited charm as Matt Murdock and relentless physical stunts as his superhero alter ego, ruling the actor out immediately is a shame — particularly now his crime-fighting days may be nearing an end with Disney's culling of Daredevil: Born Again…

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever review: The first proper MMO adventure I've been on in years
items.summary:
World of Warcraft: Forever has, much as the original World of Warcraft did back in 2004, completely consumed my life. I write about games for a living, mind, so the attention vortex it has wrought upon me is primarily professional obligation, rather than just irresponsibility. 

Need to know What is it?: A reimagining of 2004's World of Warcraft, with new balancing, lighting, dungeons, and items.
 Expect to pay: A monthly subscription of $14.99/£10.99. Optional race and early-game zone behind a £25.99/$30 paywall.
 Developer: Blizzard Entertainment
 Publisher: Blizzard Entertainment
 Reviewed on: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060, AMD Ryzen 7 5800 8-Core Processor, 16GB RAM, Force MP600 SSD
 Multiplayer?: Yes 
 Link: Official site 

But at the time of writing, it has been 443 hours since Forever's launch. I have spent 147 of those hours asleep (less, but let's just pretend I've been getting a solid eight), leaving around 296 hours of my waking mind. 230 of them have been spent playing World of Warcraft.

That's a deeply concerning amount of time if I wasn't getting a salary to review it—it has been part of my 9-5. I've also often been keeping the game open while I, you know, feed and bathe myself and do chores. So we're probably just in the realm of 'moderately worrying' rather than 'cause for a wellness check'. 

Don't worry, I intend to take a break soon: But during those 230 hours, I have hit level 60, entered 31 dungeons, completed 941 quests, levelled engineering, mining, and first aid to 300, and apparently /waved at other players 50 times. Which are rookie numbers that I need…

items.title: Should you choose the cut or pure drugs in GTA 6?
items.summary:
(Image credit: Rockstar) Deciding whether to take the cut or pure drugs in GTA 6 is a decision you'll make during the Dealer's Choice mission in Chapter 3. 

The proposal is that if you can pass off the drugs cut with baby powder, you can keep the profit, but the deal might go south if they realise, while bringing the pure stuff should make the dealers happy. Here's what happens if you choose either:

Cut drugs : If you choose the cut drugs, the dealers will immediately realise the stuff is cut with baby powder. They'll confront you, at which point you can either offer to give them half off (which reduces your profit to the same as it would have been if you'd taken pure), or you can tell them to take it or leave it. This second option will cause a gunfight, but assuming you survive, you can grab the money from their car and make maximum profit. This also doesn't have any other consequences. Pure drugs : If you choose this option, you'll make less money, but the deal will go off without a hitch after they test it. That means no gunfights. With that in mind, I'd say the cut drugs are the best to pick. You get maximum profit, a cool shootout that makes the mission less boring, and it doesn't have any significant consequences afterwards.

items.title: Dragon Age's former boss explains that poor management from EA led to BioWare shutting down because 'the options on the table were all terrible'

Last month we got the devastating news that BioWare, the legendary studio that brought us Mass Effect , Dragon Age , and classics like Neverwinter Nights , Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic , and the OG Baldur's Gate was being shut down . 

The decision was made by EA, just a year after it was acquired by a consortium made up of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and investment firms Silver Lake and Affinity Partners (owned by the son-in-law of US president Donald Trump, Jared Kushner). 

(Image credit: EA) The reasons? Underperforming games. Dragon Age: The Veilguard didn't hit the mark, Andromeda wasn't well received, and Anthem, the live-service shooter, shut its servers down for good earlier this year. 

It's a bad string of events for sure, but former Dragon Age boss Mark Darrah doesn't believe that it's all down to BioWare's poor management. The studio was backed into a corner by EA and the pressure to perform. 

Decisions like using the Frostbite Engine, "making Dragon Age 2", and "shipping Anthem" were all products of BioWare needing to hit financial targets set out by EA. "They basically said 'Gotta hit your financials, so what are you going to do?' Darrah says. "'Are you going to ship KOTOR a year sooner than you think is going to happen? No. Are you going to pull Mass Effect in a year? No. It was never clear what the consequence of 'no' was, and it still isn't. But it seemed really dire at the time. So you gotta do something, so what are you going to do? Did they make us make Dragon Age 2? No. But they made us do something."

items.title: Blade Runner 2099 Review
items.summary:
All eight episodes of Blade Runner 2099 debut on Prime Video on November 25. This is a spoiler-free review. 

There’s a scene in 2017’s Blade Runner 2049 where the very grim and serious Agent K (Ryan Gosling) makes a joke about a Wallace Corp. employee’s lost baby pictures. “Well, it’s a shame… you must’ve been adorable,” K says straight-faced. It’s a moment of levity in a pretty heavy movie, with Gosling playing it without even cracking a smile, and it works wonderfully to keep us afloat amid all the darkness – as do several other such instances in the film.

The people behind Blade Runner 2099, the latest installment in the series which began with the 1982 Ridley Scott/Harrison Ford movie , don’t understand this, or at the very least don’t think they need to include such moments of humor or lightness in their new show. As a result, watching Blade Runner 2099 very quickly turns into a slog, leading to an increasing feeling with each passing episode that the show is crushing inward on you like the teeming, downtrodden masses of its futuristic Los Angeles.

It’s not just the oh-so-serious scripting that leads to this unforced error, however. 2099 also suffers from the performances of leads Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer, who seem to be trying to out-gloom each other for most of these eight episodes. The result is a buddy-cop story where the cops not only aren’t buddies, but are also unappealing and ultimately a drag to be around. Where’s Harrison Ford and his noodles when you need them!?

items.title: Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"
items.summary:
1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project , adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many : the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

In much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise new players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered , thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the "immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the process.
items.t: Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"

items.title: 'The System Is Not Good Vs. Evil': Why GTA 6's Criminal Profile Mechanic Is Dividing Fans
items.summary:
GTA 6 players are debating the game's Criminal Profile scale, and how it operates with more depth than just a straightforward "good vs. evil" morality system.

While previous Rockstar adventures have operated on a simpler, binary scale, GTA 6 offers a more nuanced Criminal Profile that reflects your playstyle — from silent and stealthy to excessively violent and "psycho." But some players have criticised how the gameplay mechanic appears to penalise actions taken in self-defence, while others have suggested it is just not well explained.

From "Professional" all the way to "Irredeemable," GTA 6 tracks each character's actions across a series of five profile labels — and yes, you can make Jason and Lucia have wildly different personalities from each other, depending on your actions as either. But Professional does not mean pacifist, and players will inevitably still rack up a fair body count as they explore more of Leonida — the difference here is how messy you are along the way.

The scale begins with Professional, which reflects actions that align with an undetected or non-lethal play style. Stealth takedowns and non-lethal incapacitations award a focus boost, as do kind acts towards NPCs. Go for limbs (highlighted in yellow while in bullet time) rather than headshots to keep this rating intact, or earn points back towards it if you're currently rated as more wantonly violent.

Next up is Hardened, which reflects a slightly less cautious approach to firefights and taking lives in general. You're headshotting the bad guys rather than incapacitating them, in other words,…

Sneak back towards the centre of the chop shop and turn left to find the Declasse Vamos, a black unassuming car. Hop inside, start it up, and drive out of the gate you just opened. Easy, right? GTA 1 had eight selectable protagonists, four of whom were women, while GTA 2 for the Game Boy Color let you play protags Candy or Gretchen (along with a bunch of other men) in addition to the PlayStation game's default Claude Speed.

That vital pedantry out of the way, it's undeniable that Lucia is GTA's first female protagonist since the series became the culture-swallowing goliath it is today. In a chat with CBC's As It Happens , GTA OG Brian Baglow said he reckons it's "long, long overdue".

items.title: GTA 6 needed a dedicated team to make sure all its different body types could share animations: 'It was a huge team effort'

While GTA 6's body morphing might not go quite as far (in terms of waistband measurements) as its predecessor San Andreas—or even a game like Fable 2—it does boast extensive variety of different body shapes among its cast, and making that work at such a high level of visual fidelity took an entire dedicated team.

In an interview with IGN , Rockstar vice president of animation Mark Tennant said it was an early decision in development to "push the variation in character sizes and body types … This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat."

It also took eschewing a "traditional approach" in favor of "new techniques," the sort I imagine you can only implement at Rockstar levels of budget and manpower. "We also had to grow a team dedicated to overseeing the implementation, which required close collaboration with the art and rigging teams," said Tennant. If you've played League of Legends or Deadlock, it fills a niche similar to the Rift Herald or Deadlock's Unstable Rifts—an objective you can complete in the earlier stages of a game to push lane(s) hard.

items.title: GTA 6 discourse is suffering from the flat earther effect
items.summary:
If you ever watch science videos on social media, you've probably been served a video of someone debunking the claims of a flat earther.

It starts with a clip of some belligerent dope demanding to know why, if the earth is so round, ships don't disappear over the horizon. A greenscreened science communicator then appears, rubs their forehead, and shows us a video of a ship disappearing over the horizon. Checkmate. 

It's good content, but if you linger too long on one of those videos, you'll get another, and then another, and pretty soon your whole feed will be debunking videos. Now you're enrolled in a never ending lesson plan which features such insights as 'an all-meat diet is not good for you,' 'the moon landing was real,' and 'hating women is not in fact based .'

The total effect of this is that the most ignorant and dishonest quacks and provocateurs get to set the level of discourse, and instead of investigating new metaphorical horizons in topics that interest you, you wind up watching people debate the existence of the actual horizon.

Which brings me to Grand Theft Auto 6. Despite making $3.79 billion on its launch day, it's easy to stumble across confident social media claims that it's a total flop and everyone's going to refund it. According to popular X posts, GTA 6 doesn't even let you steal cars anymore, and there are hundreds of Metacritic user reviewers insisting that it's far-left propaganda rather than the mass-market entertainment product it obviously is.

It's the videogame discourse version of flat eartherism. The millions of people playing GTA 6 do…
items.t: GTA 6 discourse is suffering from the flat earther effect

items.summary:

(Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Playing on school computers has been a rite of passage for many young PC gamers, whether through dedicated edutainment titles or rogue installations by chancing pupils. But fantasy novelist Scott Lynch went one step further: he took the school computers home.

"My mother worked for our school district, so I'd occasionally have the chance to sneak into the computer lab, or we would borrow and Apple II over the summer," Lynch says. "When we did that, I borrowed Infocom games … text-only adventure games from the '80s like Zork, Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Planetfall, A Mind Forever voyaging. I was really into those when I was about 12."

Text-based adventures would eventually become a defining feature of Lynch's life, albeit in a different format. His debut novel, The Lies of Locke Lamora , was published in 2006, charting the schemes and adventures of a group of master con artists called The Gentleman Bastards. Two further novels in The Gentleman Bastard Sequence have since followed: 2007's Red Seas Under Red Skies , and 2013's The Republic of Thieves
